title: Ramayana Crosses Rs 900 Crore Worldwide in First Week as Day 7 Beats Opening Day
excerpt: Sacnilk estimates put Day 7 India net at Rs 70.65 crore — above the opening day — with India net past Rs 500 crore and overseas gross at about Rs 323.50 crore.
body:
• Ramayana: Part 1 crossed Rs 900 crore in worldwide gross in its first week, with trade trackers putting the seven-day total between roughly Rs 906 crore and Rs 935 crore.
  • On Day 7 (Wednesday, November 11), the film earned Rs 70.65 crore net in India by Sacnilk's estimates — more than its Rs 64.85 crore opening day — taking India net past Rs 500 crore.
  • Overseas markets contributed about Rs 323.50 crore gross in the first week, according to Sacnilk figures reported by the Daily Jagran.
  • The Hindi-language mythological epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1 has closed its first week past Rs 900 crore in worldwide gross, a first-week pace no Hindi film has set before it. Trade trackers differ on the exact figure — estimates for the seven-day worldwide total range from about Rs 906 crore to Rs 935 crore — but every tracker agrees the film crossed Rs 900 crore on Day 7, Wednesday, November 11.

By Sacnilk's estimates, reported by the Daily Jagran, the film earned Rs 70.65 crore net in India on Day 7 — higher than its Rs 64.85 crore opening day, a rare seventh-day rise powered by the Bhai Dooj holiday period. That took the film's India net total to Rs 511.10 crore in seven days, past the Rs 500 crore mark.

Where the money came from

India supplied Rs 611.05 crore of gross collections in the first week on the same Sacnilk tally, while overseas markets added Rs 323.50 crore gross, including Rs 25 crore on Day 7 alone. Box Office Worldwide put the pattern slightly differently — about Rs 65 crore net on Day 7, Rs 55 crore of it from the Hindi version and Rs 10 crore from the dubbed southern versions — and the worldwide gross at more than Rs 925 crore. All figures are trade estimates; final totals vary by tracker.

The film

Ramayana: Part 1 is a Hindi-language mythological epic, released with dubbed versions, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita and Yash plays Ravana. The first instalment opened in theatres on November 5, and the second part is scheduled for Diwali 2028.

What it means for the diaspora audience

The overseas share — roughly a third of the worldwide gross — underlines how much of this run is being carried by diaspora audiences in North America, the UK, the Gulf and Australia, where the film became the first Hindi release to top charts in several markets in its opening week. The next milestone is mechanical: at the first week's pace, trackers expect the Rs 1,000 crore worldwide mark to fall within days. Whether the film ultimately clears its very large production cost is a separate question the second week will begin to answer — but as a theatrical event for Indian audiences worldwide, the first week has no recent precedent.
